questions.stem: The greatest of the CHOLA emperors, who conquered Lanka + parts of SE Asia, was:

options.option_text: RAJARAJA CHOLA I (985-1014) + his son RAJENDRA CHOLA I (1014-1044) — together made Cholas South + SE Asia's greatest power

questions.explanation: CHOLA EMPIRE (9th-13th c. CE) — TAMIL dynasty ruling from THANJAVUR; one of the LONGEST-ruling dynasties in world history (reviving from 9th c.). GREATEST RULERS: (1) RAJARAJA CHOLA I (985-1014) — original name Arulmozhivarman; 'Rajaraja' = 'King of Kings'. Conquered (a) Pandyas of Madurai, (b) Cheras of Kerala, (c) Western Chalukyas, (d) Sri Lanka (northern, incl. Anuradhapura — renamed 'Mummudi Chola Mandalam'), (e) Maldives (first Indian empire to conquer beyond South Asia). Built THE BRIHADESHVARA TEMPLE (Rajarajeshwaram) at THANJAVUR (1010 CE) — UNESCO World Heritage; 66m tall vimana; one of India's tallest temples; 80-tonne granite capstone on top; 130-ton Nandi; massive stone carved. Undertook great LAND SURVEY + centralised revenue. (2) RAJENDRA CHOLA I (1014-1044) — son + successor; EXPANDED further. Defeated PALAS of Bengal (Mahipala); marched to GANGES + took Ganges water home — built GANGAIKONDACHOLAPURAM (new capital); took title 'Gangaikonda' (conqueror of Ganges) + 'Kadaram-kondan' (conqueror of Kadaram). NAVAL EXPEDITION TO SOUTHEAST ASIA (1025) — defeated SRIVIJAYA EMPIRE (Malaya-Sumatra); took tribute from Kadaram (Kedah), Sri Vishaya (Palembang), Srivijaya, Pannai, Malaiyur, Mayirudingam, Ilangasoga, Mapappalam, Valaippandur, Takkola, Madamalingam, Ilamurideham, Manakkavaram (Nicobar), KADARAM — across Malaysia, Indonesia, Myanmar. FIRST INDIAN MARITIME EMPIRE of substance. Built CHOLAMANDALAM (Coromandel Coast). PATRONISED ART + literature — Tamil Bhakti (Tevaram saints canonised under him); 63 Nayanar + 12 Alvar hymns; Nataraja bronzes peak. (3) KULOTTUNGA I (1070-1122), RAJENDRA II, KULOTTUNGA III maintained empire till 1279 when PANDYAS overran.

questions.stem: The BRIHADESHVARA TEMPLE at THANJAVUR (a UNESCO World Heritage site) was built by:

options.option_text: RAJARAJA CHOLA I (completed 1010 CE) — dedicated to Lord Shiva; part of 'Great Living Chola Temples' UNESCO site

questions.explanation: BRIHADESHVARA TEMPLE / 'RajaRajeswaram' / 'Peruvudaiyar Kovil' at THANJAVUR (Tanjore), Tamil Nadu — ARCHITECTURAL MARVEL of CHOLA era. BUILT by RAJARAJA CHOLA I; completed in 1010 CE. DEDICATED to LORD SHIVA. FEATURES: (1) VIMANA (tower above sanctum) — 66 METRES (216 ft) tall, made of granite — one of the tallest in India; (2) capped by a single 80-tonne granite stone (some say 130 tonnes via ramp up a 6km earthen slope per legend); (3) LARGE NANDI (monolithic seated bull) — 6 m long, 2.7 m tall, 360 tonnes; (4) SANCTUM houses a 3.7m Shiva lingam; (5) fresco paintings in Chola + later Nayak layers on walls; (6) inscriptions in Tamil + Grantha detailing the temple's administration, donations, dancing girls (devadasis — 400 employed), staff, grants. Financed by tribute + loot from Rajaraja's conquests. UNESCO listed 1987 as part of 'GREAT LIVING CHOLA TEMPLES' group with two others: (a) BRIHADESHVARA at GANGAIKONDACHOLAPURAM (built by Rajendra Chola c. 1035 CE to celebrate his Ganges victory — slightly smaller but more ornate); (b) AIRAVATESHVARA TEMPLE at DARASURAM (built by Rajaraja II c. 1166 CE). All 3 showcase DRAVIDA architectural style at peak. DRAVIDA (SOUTHERN) vs NAGARA (NORTHERN) vs VESARA (HYBRID) are 3 Indian temple styles (classified in Shilpa texts). DRAVIDA features: (a) square/rectangular plan; (b) TALL vimana above garbha-griha (sanctum); (c) PYRAMIDAL + tiered vimana; (d) GOPURAMS (gateway towers) at cardinal entrances (became increasingly tall, surpassing vimana in later centuries); (e) COMPOUND walls with multiple courts; (f) MANDAPAS (pillared halls); (g) temple TANK (kalyani); (h) Dravidian stupi (finial). Famous Dravida temples: Pallava (Kailasanatha Kanchipuram), Chola (Brihadeshvara), Chalukya (Badami), Pandya (Meenakshi Madurai), Vijayanagar (Hampi), Nayak era (Meenakshi + Ranganathaswamy Srirangam).

questions.stem: The CHOLA local government had a highly developed VILLAGE ASSEMBLY system. The assembly of a Brahmadeya (Brahmin-settled village) was called:

options.option_text: SABHA / MAHASABHA — elected by Kudavolai (lottery/pot) system; UTTIRAMERUR inscriptions (c. 919 CE) detail procedure + qualifications

questions.explanation: CHOLA LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT — one of the most developed systems of medieval world. THREE TYPES of village assemblies: (1) UR — regular village of non-Brahmin cultivators; general assembly of all adult male landholders. (2) SABHA / MAHASABHA — assembly of BRAHMADEYA (Brahmin-settled village); exclusively for learned Brahmins + involved complex elected committees. (3) NAGARAM — assembly of merchant towns; like NAGARATTAR commercial guilds. UTTIRAMERUR INSCRIPTIONS (c. 919 CE, near Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu) by PARANTAKA CHOLA I — detail elaborate ELECTION PROCEDURE of SABHA: (a) Qualifications — (i) own land of 1/4 veli; (ii) reside in own house on that land; (iii) age 35-70; (iv) knowledge of Vedas + Dharmashastra; (v) honest + good character. (b) Disqualifications — embezzlers of public funds, those with close relatives in office, defaulters of taxes. (c) Selection by KUDAVOLAI ('pot ticket' — LOTTERY) system: names written on palm-leaf tickets, placed in pot, a young priest drew names; rotation ensured broad participation; prevented oligarchy. (d) 30 wards of village → 30 members chosen annually. (e) 6 VARIYAM (committees) — Samvatsara-variyam (annual committee), Totta-variyam (garden committee), Eri-variyam (TANK committee — maintenance of IRRIGATION tank was sacred!), Pancha-vara-variyam (standing committee of 5), Pon-variyam (gold committee / treasury), Nyaya-variyam (justice committee). (f) 1-YEAR term; those who committed fraud disqualified for life + 7 generations. REMARKABLE for: (1) PRESCRIBED qualifications + DISQUALIFICATIONS; (2) secret ballot / lottery — innovative for 10th c.; (3) PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY — regular audit; (4) committees for SPECIFIC FUNCTIONS. Dr B.R. AMBEDKAR + framers of Indian Constitution studied this system for PANCHAYATI RAJ — Art 40 DPSP. UTTIRAMERUR remains a PILGRIMAGE of DEMOCRACY. Cholas' decentralised governance = secret of long rule.

questions.stem: The CHOLA BRONZES (lost-wax cast bronze figures) are most famously represented by:

options.option_text: NATARAJA (Shiva as cosmic dancer in TANDAVA pose) — CHIDAMBARAM; now iconic symbol of Indian art globally

questions.explanation: CHOLA BRONZES — unrivalled tradition of Lost-wax casting (Cire Perdue / Madhuchchhishta Vidhana) that peaked during 10th-12th centuries. MOST ICONIC: NATARAJA ('King of Dance') — Shiva as cosmic dancer performing the TANDAVA. ATTRIBUTES: (1) 4 ARMS — upper right holds DAMARU (drum, creation + sound/time), upper left holds AGNI (fire, destruction + transformation), lower right in ABHAYA mudra (fear-not / protection), lower left points to raised foot (moksha / liberation); (2) raised LEFT foot — 'raising of consciousness'; (3) right foot CRUSHING APASMARA (dwarf-demon of ignorance); (4) dancing within a PRABHAMANDALA (circle of FIRE) representing the cosmos; (5) JATAMUKUTA (dread-locks flowing); (6) GANGA in hair; (7) snake around waist; (8) 'ANANDATANDAVA' = dance of bliss. LOCATION: primary Nataraja shrine = CHIDAMBARAM (Tamil Nadu), one of Panch Bhoota Sthalams representing AKASHA (space/ether); Nataraja in temple gold-plated; called 'Thillai Nataraja'. PHILOSOPHICAL: symbolises 5 cosmic activities of Shiva (Panchakritya) — creation, preservation, destruction, concealment, liberation. Universal symbol — CERN's Geneva campus has a Nataraja statue (donated by India 2004) honoring the 'cosmic dance' analogy with particle physics. OTHER CHOLA BRONZES: Parvati (Uma), Shiva-Parvati-Skanda (Somaskanda), Rama-Sita-Lakshmana (Ram-setu), Krishna, saints (Nayanars, Alvars — 63 canonised under Rajaraja), dancing Shiva variants. CASTING TECHNIQUE: (1) wax model sculpted; (2) coated in clay; (3) heated to melt wax out ('lost wax'); (4) molten bronze poured in; (5) clay broken + bronze cleaned. Each piece UNIQUE. Chola bronzes display perfect ANATOMICAL precision + graceful contrapposto; IDEALISED proportions per SILPA SHASTRA; incredible realism + sinuous motion. MODERN MUSEUMS: Govt Museum Chennai, Thanjavur Royal Art Gallery, National Museum Delhi, British Museum, Louvre, MET NYC, Asian Civilisations Museum Singapore — all have Chola bronzes. India has SEIZED BACK many looted Chola bronzes (Suthamalli Nataraja 2015, Sripuranthan Nataraja 2015 — from Australia, US smugglers).

questions.stem: The three MAJOR SOUTH INDIAN DYNASTIES of the Sangam Age (3rd c. BCE – 3rd c. CE) were:

options.option_text: CHERAS (Kerala + W.TN), CHOLAS (central + E.TN Cauvery delta), PANDYAS (southern TN, Madurai)

questions.explanation: THREE CROWNED KINGS (MUVENDAR) of Sangam Age South India: (1) CHERAS (Keralaputra) — ruled KERALA + western Tamil Nadu; capital VANJI / Karur; emblems: bow + arrow; greatest king SENGUTTUVAN (the Cheran warrior-prince who invaded north India per Silappadikaram). (2) CHOLAS — central + eastern Tamil Nadu (CAUVERY Delta, Thanjavur region); capital URAIYUR (Tiruchirapalli); emblem: tiger; greatest king KARIKALA (built Grand Anicut / Kallanai dam on Kaveri — one of world's oldest working dams, still in use!). (3) PANDYAS — southern Tamil Nadu; capital MADURAI; emblem: fish; patrons of TAMIL SANGAMS (literary academies) — 3 Sangams in Madurai, 1st + 2nd mythical, 3rd (c. 3 BCE-3 CE) historical; Pandyas = 'PERUMBANARRUPPADAI' + TAMIL SANGAM patrons. SANGAM LITERATURE — ETTUTHOKAI (Eight Anthologies: Natrinai, Kurunthokai, Ainkurunuru, Padirrupathu, Paripadal, Kalithokai, Akananuru, Purananuru), PATTUPATTU (Ten Idylls), TOLKAPPIYAM (earliest Tamil grammar by Tolkappiyar, ~3rd c. BCE). 5 TINAI (ecological regions) — Kurinji (hill), Mullai (pastoral), Marudam (cropland), Neydal (coast), Palai (desert). TRADE: Tamil Nadu's ARIKAMEDU (near Puducherry) was major ROMAN TRADE PORT (1st-2nd c. CE) — Roman coins, amphorae, rouletted ware, pottery found; mentioned in Periplus of the Erythraean Sea + Ptolemy as 'Poduke'. Tamil ports — Muziris (Kerala, Cranganore/Kodungallur), Korkai, Kaveripoompattinam/Puhar. Exports: spices (pepper, cardamom, cinnamon), pearls, gems, silk, teak, peacocks; imports: Roman gold + wine. Sangam era ENDED ~3rd c. CE (Kalabhra interregnum) → MEDIEVAL Cholas (Vijayalaya 848 CE), PALLAVAS (Kanchi), PANDYAS (revival) emerged. CHENNAI + MADURAI remain ancient urban centres. Sangam age epics: SILAPPADIKARAM (story of Kannagi + Kovalan), MANIMEKALAI (Buddhist sequel), CHIVAKA CHINTAMANI (Jain).

questions.stem: The PALLAVA dynasty, who ruled from KANCHIPURAM (4th-9th c. CE), is credited with:

options.option_text: Founding ROCK-CUT + STRUCTURAL temple architecture in South India — MAHABALIPURAM monuments (UNESCO); KAILASANATHA Kanchipuram

questions.explanation: PALLAVA DYNASTY (c. 275-897 CE) — Tamil dynasty ruling NORTHERN Tamil Nadu + parts of AP from KANCHIPURAM. Initiated DRAVIDA TEMPLE ARCHITECTURE evolution. FOUR PHASES of Pallava art: (1) MAHENDRA group (7th c.) — rock-cut cave temples. (2) NARASIMHA group / MAHABALIPURAM — monolithic ratha temples + bas-reliefs. (3) RAJASIMHA / STRUCTURAL period — first free-standing structural temples (Shore Temple, Kailasanatha). (4) NANDIVARMAN / LATER Pallava. KEY RULERS: (1) MAHENDRAVARMAN I (600-630) — scholar-king, author of 'MATTAVILASA PRAHASANA' (Sanskrit satirical drama); initial rock-cut caves; converted from Jainism to Shaivism under Appar. (2) NARASIMHAVARMAN I 'MAMALLA' (630-668) — defeated Chalukya PULAKESIN II in epic battles; founded MAHABALIPURAM / MAMALLAPURAM port; built Pancha Rathas (5 monolithic temples carved from single rocks — Dharmaraja, Bhima, Arjuna, Draupadi, Nakul-Sahadeva Rathas). (3) RAJASIMHA / NARASIMHAVARMAN II (700-728) — built the SHORE TEMPLE at Mahabalipuram + KAILASANATHA TEMPLE at Kanchipuram. (4) NANDIVARMAN II (731-796) — built VAIKUNTHA PERUMAL temple. MAHABALIPURAM (Mamallapuram) — UNESCO WHS 1984. Monuments: (a) SHORE TEMPLE — 8th c., two shikharas, oceanfront, battered by cyclones; (b) FIVE RATHAS (Pancha Rathas) — monoliths, each different Dravida temple form; (c) ARJUNA'S PENANCE / Descent of the Ganga — massive open-air BAS-RELIEF (27m × 9m) — one of the world's largest; (d) cave temples — Varaha, Mahishasuramardini, Trimurti, Krishna; (e) KRISHNA'S BUTTERBALL — precariously balanced granite boulder. KANCHIPURAM — 'City of 1000 Temples'; KAILASANATHA TEMPLE (Rajasimha) — earliest structural temple; Vaikuntha Perumal; Ekambareshwara; Varadaraja; Kamakshi Amman. Kanchipuram also a major BUDDHIST + JAIN centre; seat of Shankaracharya MATHA (one of the four original). ENDED by CHOLAS — ADITYA I defeated last Pallava APARAJITAVARMAN at TIRUPPURAMBIYAM (897 CE). Pallavas influenced CAMBODIA + INDONESIA — Shailendra + Khmer temples derive from Pallava grammar.

questions.stem: The GRAND ANICUT (Kallanai), one of the world's OLDEST functioning dams, was built on the Kaveri River (~150 CE) by:

options.option_text: KARIKALA CHOLA — early Chola king of the Sangam age; dam still in use 2000 years later near Trichy

questions.explanation: GRAND ANICUT / KALLANAI — ~2000-year-old DAM + diversion weir on the KAVERI (Cauvery) river, near TIRUCHIRAPPALLI (Trichy), Tamil Nadu. Built by KARIKALA CHOLA (~150 CE), early Chola of the Sangam age. STRUCTURE: originally a rubble-masonry weir, 329m long × 20m wide × 5m deep; designed to divert Kaveri's waters to irrigate Thanjavur delta — 'rice bowl of South India'. Still FUNCTIONS TODAY (after many renovations — British in 1804 by Sir Arthur Cotton who studied Kallanai + adapted its design for his Godavari + Krishna deltas; modern concrete reinforcement). One of the OLDEST WATER-REGULATION structures in the world still in use. Irrigates ~400,000 hectares today. KARIKALA CHOLA — early Chola king; famous for defeating Cheras + Pandyas (Venni battle); credited with: (a) building Kallanai; (b) felling forests + bringing large tracts under rice cultivation; (c) founding Puhar (Kaveripoompattinam) as port; (d) building grand palace at Uraiyur. Mentioned in SANGAM LITERATURE (Pattinappalai by Kadialur Uruttirangannanar describes his Puhar's splendor). ORIGIN LEGEND: 'Karikala' = 'charred leg' — burned as an infant. Known as 'Tiruvalangadan' + great warrior + visionary ruler. OTHER ANCIENT INDIAN DAMS + IRRIGATION: (1) SUDARSHANA LAKE at Girnar, Gujarat — built by CHANDRAGUPTA MAURYA's governor PUSHYAGUPTA (~321 BCE); repaired by Ashoka + later Rudradaman (rock inscription 150 CE) + Skandagupta — celebrated Junagadh Rock Inscription. (2) HAUZ KHAS (Alauddin's reservoir) + HAUZ-I-SULTANI + Firoz Shah's canals. (3) HALEBIDU + HOYSALA tanks in Karnataka. (4) Kakatiya tanks in Telangana — PAKHAL, LAKNAVARAM, Ramappa — UNESCO since 2021 ('Kakatiya Rudreshwara Ramappa Temple'). (5) Mughal canal on Yamuna (Firoz Shah's revived by Shah Jahan's Ali Mardan Khan). Indian water-management expertise is OLD + DEEP.

questions.stem: The CHALUKYAS of BADAMI (6th-8th c.) reached their peak under which king?

options.option_text: PULAKESIN II (609-642) — defeated HARSHA at Narmada (630); received emissaries from Persia; eventually defeated by Pallava Narasimhavarman I

questions.explanation: CHALUKYAS OF BADAMI / VATAPI (543-757 CE) — Kannada dynasty ruling from BADAMI (modern Bagalkot district, KARNATAKA). Greatest ruler: PULAKESIN II (609-642) — perhaps the most powerful Deccan king of his time. ACHIEVEMENTS: (1) defeated HARSHA of Kanauj at NARMADA (~630 CE) — Harsha stopped at Narmada, Deccan remained independent; Pulakesin assumed title 'Dakshinapatheswara' ('Lord of South'); 'Maharajadhiraja'. (2) Defeated Pallavas repeatedly; took Kanchi (briefly). (3) Received emissary from KHUSRAU II of PERSIAN SASSANID Empire (Ajanta cave 1 has a famous painting depicting this); sent one to Khusrau. (4) Conquered Gujarat, parts of MP. (5) Chinese traveller HIUEN TSANG (Xuanzang, 631 CE) visited his court; praised his just rule. LIMITS: eventually DEFEATED + KILLED by Pallava NARASIMHAVARMAN I 'MAMALLA' at Vatapi (642 CE) — hence 'Vatapi-kondan' title of Pallava. BADAMI TEMPLES: (a) 4 Rock-Cut Cave temples (Vaishnavite, Shaivite, Jain), 6th-7th c., early Dravida + Nagara fusion; (b) AIHOLE — 125+ temples (6th-9th c.), 'cradle of Hindu temple architecture' — Durga temple, Lad Khan temple, Ravana Phadi cave; (c) PATTADAKAL — 10 temples of later Chalukyas (UNESCO since 1987), Virupaksha temple mahalayas. LATER CHALUKYAS: (1) WESTERN CHALUKYAS of KALYANI (973-1189) — dynasty revived by Tailapa II; greatest king VIKRAMADITYA VI (1076-1126) — started Chalukya-Vikrama era. Court poet BILHANA (Vikramankadevacharita), jurist VIJNANESWARA (Mitakshara — classical Hindu law commentary, still used in legal reference). (2) EASTERN CHALUKYAS of VENGI (624-1189) — ruled coastal Andhra; branch founded by Kubja Vishnuvardhana, brother of Pulakesin II; Telugu literature flowered under them — NANNAYA's Mahabharata (11th c.). (3) CHALUKYAS of GUJARAT / Solanki (950-1300) — separate. Chalukyas succeeded by RASHTRAKUTAS (753-982) who defeated Badami Chalukyas. DANTIDURGA founded Rashtrakuta; AMOGHAVARSHA I (814-878) — great Rashtrakuta king, author of 'Kavirajamarga' (earliest Kannada poetics); Jain patron; Sanskrit + Kannada literature flowered. ELLORA's Kailasa Temple (rock-cut, monolithic, 8th c.) built by Rashtrakuta KRISHNA I — a pinnacle of Indian architecture.

questions.stem: The famous KAILASA TEMPLE (Cave 16) at ELLORA — carved from a SINGLE ROCK top-down — was commissioned by:

options.option_text: RASHTRAKUTA king KRISHNA I (757-773) — monolithic rock-cut temple, single largest stone excavation ever; 200,000 tonnes of basalt removed

questions.explanation: KAILASA TEMPLE (Cave 16 of ELLORA caves, AURANGABAD district, MAHARASHTRA) — one of the most astonishing architectural feats of ANCIENT INDIA; considered one of the greatest monolithic structures in world. COMMISSIONED by RASHTRAKUTA KING KRISHNA I (757-773 CE). DEDICATED to Lord SHIVA, representing MT KAILASA (Shiva's abode). STRUCTURE: carved from a SINGLE block of BASALT rock, TOP-DOWN (starting from top + excavating downward + inward); ~2,00,000 TONNES of rock removed; estimated ~150 years of continuous labour. DIMENSIONS: 30 m tall, 46 m wide, 82 m long. FEATURES: (1) Free-standing structural form despite being monolithic; (2) 2-storey GOPURAM entrance; (3) NANDI mandapa; (4) FIVE subsidiary shrines representing Mt Meru; (5) 16-pillared MAHAMANDAPA; (6) GARBHA-GRIHA (sanctum) with Shivalingam; (7) Elaborate SCULPTURES including RAVANA shaking Mt Kailasa (Ravananugrahamurti), Mahishasuramardini, Dashavatara, epic scenes from Ramayana + Mahabharata + Puranas. ELLORA CAVES — UNESCO WHS 1983 — 34 CAVES along 2km basalt cliff: (1) Caves 1-12 = BUDDHIST (6th-7th c.) — Vishwakarma (chaitya with stupa), Tin Thal (3-storeyed); (2) Caves 13-29 = HINDU (7th-10th c.) — Kailasa, Dasavatara, Rameshwara; (3) Caves 30-34 = JAIN (8th-10th c.) — Indra Sabha, Jagannatha Sabha, Chota Kailasa. UNIQUE RELIGIOUS COEXISTENCE — Buddhist, Hindu, Jain shrines side-by-side showing medieval religious pluralism. AJANTA CAVES (MH, Aurangabad — UNESCO WHS 1983) — 30 cave temples (Buddhist only, 2nd c. BCE to 6th c. CE) — famous for MURAL PAINTINGS (Jataka tales, Bodhisattvas; 'Padmapani' + 'Vajrapani' in Cave 1). Rediscovered 1819 by British hunting officer Captain John Smith. AJANTA + ELLORA together = the 2 wondrous rock-cut traditions of India. OTHER major rock-cut sites: Elephanta (Maharashtra, UNESCO 1987); Bagh (MP); Badami (Karnataka); Mahabalipuram (TN); Udayagiri-Khandagiri (Odisha); Bhaja, Karle, Bedse (MH).

questions.stem: The VIJAYANAGAR EMPIRE (1336-1646) was founded by:

options.option_text: HARIHARA + BUKKA (Sangama brothers) in 1336, with guidance of sage VIDYARANYA — as bulwark against Delhi Sultanate southern expansion

questions.explanation: VIJAYANAGAR EMPIRE (1336-1646) — great Hindu empire of SOUTH INDIA; bulwark against Bahmani + Delhi Sultanate southward expansion; capital HAMPI (modern Karnataka, UNESCO WHS 1986). FOUNDED in 1336 by two brothers: HARIHARA I + BUKKA (SANGAMA BROTHERS), per tradition with spiritual guidance of sage VIDYARANYA (of Sringeri Math) — 'Vidyanagara' (city of learning), renamed VIJAYANAGAR ('city of victory'). Brothers had been captured by Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq, forcibly converted to Islam, then sent back south to quell rebellions; Vidyaranya reconverted them back to Hinduism — they founded the empire instead. FOUR DYNASTIES: (1) SANGAMA (1336-1485) — founders; Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Bukka II, Devaraya I + II. (2) SALUVA (1485-1505) — founded by Saluva Narasimha; short-lived. (3) TULUVA (1505-1570) — the GOLDEN AGE; KRISHNADEVARAYA (1509-1529) — emperor par excellence; poet, patron, conqueror; defeated Bahmani sultans, Gajapatis of Orissa; built HAZARA RAMA temple + VITTALA temple. Author of 'AMUKTAMALYADA' (Telugu — advice-cum-love-story on ideal kingship + 8 duties). Court of 'ASHTADIGGAJAS' (8 poets) — Allasani Peddana (Andhra-Kavita-Pitamaha, 'grandfather of Telugu poetry'), Nandi Timmana, Mukku Timmana, Madayyagari Mallana, Pingali Surana (Kalapurnodayam), Dhurjati, Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu, Ramaraja Bhushanudu (Bhattumurti). (4) ARAVIDU (1570-1646) — last dynasty; after BATTLE OF TALIKOTA (23 Jan 1565) where combined DECCAN SULTANATES (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar) DESTROYED Vijayanagar forces + RAMA RAYA killed; Hampi razed over 6 months. Empire limped on from Penukonda + Chandragiri till 1646. HAMPI is a UNESCO WHS — spectacular ruins, Vittala temple with STONE CHARIOT + musical pillars (SaReGa), Virupaksha temple (still functional), Lotus Mahal, Elephant Stables, Hazara Rama, Krishna temple. Famous foreign VISITORS to Vijayanagar: Nicolo Conti (Italian 1420), Abdur Razzaq (Persian 1440-1445), Duarte Barbosa + DOMINGO PAES (Portuguese 1520-22), Fernao Nuniz (Portuguese 1530s). Paes called Hampi 'as large as Rome' + 'the best-provided city in the world'. CURRENCY: PAGODA (gold coin) + VARAHA. BANKING developed well. COROMANDEL + MALABAR trade.
